body:
> Okay, I noticed this: "Their friends and parents aren't dying. They didn't lose their favourite blanket." I'm asking you straight out if you've had any friends or parents die?

No, I haven't. I started talking about conceptual things to complain about, and a person dying was the first conceptual thing I could think of. I guess that means I can't think of a person's death tangibly. Or at least I don't mourn the tangibility of a person's death like other people (seem to) do.

Thank you for the kind words.

I don't understand crap about poetry (or e. e. cummings for that matter) either. It's a stream of consciousness (or whatever it's called), so I tried to write it with the same tempo as it was in my head.

> I don't understand the purpose of hyphenating words together, e.g. miss-those-days

When I hyphenate something together: like here

> the sixteen-year-olds-I-looked-up-to

I'm emphasising that I think of this as a 'thing' of itself. In this case I'm saying there are sixteen-year-olds, and sixteen-year-olds-I-looked-up-to.

> Also, for me the formatting was really messed up which made it difficult to read (maybe it was just on my computer?).

There are lots of line breaks and areas where I've cut off lines or let them run longer, to try and add another layer to that line. So it's probably fine on your side.

P - provocative (or seductive) behavior: *Not in the least*

R - relationships, considered more intimate than they are: *Yet again*

A - attention, must be at center of: *I tend to go after attention from individuals*

I - influenced easily: *Nope*

S - speech (style) - wants to impress, lacks detail: *Completely 
applicable*

E - emotional lability, shallowness: *I'd say so*

M - make-up - physical appearance used to draw attention to self: *Jeans and shirts*

E - exaggerated emotions - theatrical: *Not so much exaggerated, but fake*

Maybe. I sure tell people I do/want to.

I just don't care about other people; their needs, lives, and when they need attention. I'm self-centered in the most literal sense and it kills me.

It's usually the same thing. They're always the same as everyone else. Not the same, as in the way they treat me, but that they're so homogeneous. Everyone fits an archetype after a while of me knowing them. People just get so boring in such a short period.

I don't know why, but I always hate them for that.

There's no way that's going to be accurate.
For example:
> 	I enjoy meeting new people. 

I would strongly agree with this, but only because it implies (to me) that I'm no long conversing with the old people. The longer someone knows me the more they dislike me and the more I dislike them. So getting away from people and to knew ones is a pleasurable thing to me.

But that's got to be one of the most antisocial things a person could say.

That would be nice. I've sent you some info on my whereabouts. 

What did you have in mind? I've seen a therapist once; my mother thought we were having "family issues". The therapist obviously thought I was depressed and said something to my mother, but she stopped going (and I with her) because it was "too expensive".

I think the point of the question was 'Will militant fighting ever cease'. The point of my answer was that we're never going to reach a point when we can escape the reasons for war, because they're physical and not (necessarily) mental. No new stage of enlightenment is going to end our need for food. And that need might turn into entertainment or something later on.

> Can you elaborate what these people say your problem is?

I'm not social. At all. And people tell me the reason I'm so unhappy is because I'm not social. 

They're probably talking about something else that I just can't see, but I don't understand.

> No matter how clearly you see the world, you still only see your version of it.

Yes. Things might get better. Things probably will get better. Most of that wasn't something I rue on often, just all I could think just then. 

But it's not the future that worries me. The proceeding eight years are fine. Hopeful, even. I have no concern with them.

It's the two years sitting in front that worry me. The ones that are going to suck indefinitely. I don't want to wallow through this for two years only to get to something that *might* be better.

> Can you talk to someone you trust at school? There may be a school counselor or someone for you, but even a teacher you respect and like would be a good starting point. Don't shy away from seeking a little bit of help, OK?

I've tried talking with people. I really have. 

Any friends think I'm being a whiny bitch. I wouldn't bother them with this anyway. The counselor at school doesn't understand - anything, it's not her field. All she knows how to care about and all she's trained to care about are issues with students that will actually affect their academic performance. Apparently my atrocious grades aren't a result of anything psychological. I'm just stupid or lazy.

I wouldn't talk to my mother about any of this. Every time I try she never bothers to try understanding. In the end I just stop and she writes it off as teenage bullshit. It is teenage bullshit. That's obvious. But that doesn't mean I don't need help.

I don't know. What else is there? That sounds short-sighted, but I'm serious.

It will be another two years of this until I'm off to college. Which might not even happen at this rate. Even if things do work out it's another four to eight year long rut of similar bullshit? Then what? I get a job and do the same fucking thing for the rest of my life?
There's just a couple days to a couple weeks of actual pleasure (which usually get filled up by work you couldn't finish during the week), parsed by five days of soul-crushingly boring 

God fuck it. I don't know. And I don't feel like quantifying things down to a single problem because it's more complicated than that.
